Investment Principles

We invest where India is going, not where it has been.

01
Tech & media reshape consumption
India has moved from secular brands. Social media has given way to create brands targeting a specific niche or a cohort
02
Old comes back in new forms
Re-imagination of familiar categories will drive the next wave.
03
Youth resist inherited patterns
The next generation wants to create their own consumption story.
04
India's pulse = opportunities
The deepest wins come from knowing Bharat beyond the metros.
05
Legacy categories are the low-hanging fruit
Redefined propositions in mature spaces win big.
06
Consumption is a profession
Today's consumers are skilled, informed and hard to fool.
07
Brands are culture keepers
Brands must create and protect culture, not merely extract from it.
08
Impermanence as a feature
Businesses of the future must be built to flex, not just scale.
09
AI redefines agility
Faster paths to growth — if you know how to use it.
The India Story

India is becoming the 3rd largest economy by 2030.

Growing at 8% annually — nearly 3x the US and Germany — India's private consumption powers 61% of nominal GDP. Beyond $2,500 per capita, discretionary income grows disproportionately, and India is hitting that inflection point right now.

The top 30 million Indian households (India-1) dominate 70-89% of value-added consumption — and this cohort is adding 30 million more households by 2030. A consumer market unlike anything the world has seen.

Our Framework

Building for India 1

India One
The Consuming Class
Those able to afford domestic help. India-1 represents the top 30 million households dominating 70-89% of value-added consumption — beverages, beauty, dining, durables, travel. Adding 30 million more by 2030.
India Two
The Serving Class
The backbone of Indian society — domestic help, drivers, shop-floor workers, delivery personnel. As India-1 grows, so does the aspirational spending of India-2. An entirely new brand cohort waiting to be served.
